findings.title: No server-owned binding precedence or pinning contract test
findings.evidence: Plan B1 lines 255-259 requires TODO > workspace > global precedence and a server-pinned active-slice binding revision. Plan A line 336 and FR-PROCESS-001 AC-001-02 require active-slice pinning. tests/ProcessContext.Tests.ps1 lines 218-237 put pins in a test-local hashtable and program the resolve callback to return those pins. The plugin adapter merely echoes that reply. No test invokes a server binding resolver or varies TODO/workspace/global assignments, ambiguity, approved change, signed migration, or active revision consistency.
findings.remediation: Write focused McpServer service-contract tests against a replaceable persistence/approval double. Assert precedence, ambiguity, active slice revision pinning across changed approved binding, new-slice selection, and unauthorized migration rejection. Run those tests in mock mode with field-specific negative controls and obtain this phase review before changing server production.

findings.title: Named BDPv4 fixture does not represent the approved BDPv4 graph
findings.evidence: tests/ProcessContext.Tests.ps1 lines 15-24 sets GraphA to requirements, mock-validated, real-green only; lines 34-49 label it BDPv4. Plan B5 line 300 declares requirements/AC ready, tests written, mock validated, real implementation allowed, real green, full suite green, hostile validation, done, and plan A line 336 requires BDPv4 plus a different approved process. The test proves passthrough of a three-node synthetic graph, not preservation of the approved graph identity and edges.
findings.remediation: Use a source-pinned, immutable BDPv4 manifest fixture with its declared phase/gate graph and a materially different second fixture. Assert exact manifest digest and graph in the adapter test, with a graph-edge mutation negative control. Avoid embedding BDP rules in production plugin code.
